questions: Should the custom encoder convert Enum instances to their name (Color.RED -> 'RED') or their value (Color.RED -> 1)?
If an Enum member has a non-serializable value (e.g., a custom object), should the encoder still try to serialize it as the value, or should it fall back to the name?
Should the encoder handle subclasses of Enum (like IntEnum, Flag) the same way as Enum?
What should happen if the input object contains a non-Enum custom class instance (e.g., a datetime) — should it raise TypeError immediately, or attempt to use the base JSONEncoder default?
Should the JSON output be formatted with any specific indentation or separators (compact vs pretty-printed)?
If an Enum is nested inside a non-dict iterable (like a tuple or set), should it still be serialized, and if so, how are those container types handled?
Should the encoder ensure ASCII-only output (ensure_ascii=True) or allow Unicode characters?
If the input is None, should it serialize to 'null' or raise an error?
